title: Extending a finite cover by normalization
statement:
Let $X$ be integral of finite type over a field, let
$V\subset X$ be a nonempty normal open, and let
$P\to V$ be connected and
finite etale.
The normalization of $X$ in $k(P)$, as in
[def-fin-normalization-extension], restricts over
$V$ to the given cover $P\to V$.

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes X Noetherian; the open V is Noetherian, and the finite morphism f:P→V makes P Noetherian. Use the finite morphism finite-type instance directly; properness is unnecessary.

source.place: Normality and normalization comparison; implemented through Mathlib relative-normalization universal property (035I) and smooth base change (03GV).

proof.text: Apply the finite clopen normal-integral component theorem to P→V. Choose a point p of the connected nonempty P and a component containing p. Its clopen underlying set is all of P by connectedness. The component inclusion is therefore the top-open isomorphism, which transports integrality and integrally closed stalks to P.

source.place: Normality and normalization comparison; implemented through Mathlib relative-normalization universal property (035I) and smooth base change (03GV).

proof.text: The composite t:P→V→X is open, so its nonempty image is dense in the integral X. The image of the generic point is consequently the generic point of X. Transport t's generic stalk map to m:k(X)→k(P); stalk-map naturality gives Spec(m);j_X=j_P;t. Take the algebra induced by m. This establishes exactly the asserted structural equality without needing a separate finite-dimensional or separability instance.

source.place: Normality and normalization comparison; implemented through Mathlib relative-normalization universal property (035I) and smooth base change (03GV).

proof.text: The absolute normalization of P is P: apply normalization over the normal locus at the top open and cancel the top-open inclusions. Put j=j_P and g=j;f. The universal property gives m:N(g)→P, with m;f=ν_g and i_g;m=j. Because m is integral, it also gives d:N(j)→N(g), with d;m=ν_j and i_j;d=i_g. Set n=ν_j^{-1};d. Then n;m=id_P. The uniqueness part of the relative-normalization universal property gives m;n=id_N(g), since both composites to V and both restrictions along i_g agree. Thus N(g)≅P over V. The same universal property transports relative normalization along any isomorphism of sources over V.

source.place: Normality and normalization comparison; implemented through Mathlib relative-normalization universal property (035I) and smooth base change (03GV).

proof.text: Let φ=Spec(k(P))→X be the structural map from step 3. Its factorization through V identifies Spec(k(P)) with Spec(k(P))×_X V by the pullback universal property and monicity of V→X. Transport relative normalization along this source isomorphism. Normalization commutes with smooth base change along the open immersion V→X, so N(φ)×_X V≅N(g). Compose with the isomorphism N(g)≅P from step 4. The equations normalizationPullback_snd and normalizationDesc_comp give exactly e.hom;f=pullback.snd, completing the statement.

lean.statement: theorem normalizationIn_functionField_extends_cover {k : Type u} [Field k] (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral X] [X.Over (Spec (.of k))] [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of k))] (V : X.Opens) [Nonempty V] (hV : IsNormalScheme V.toScheme) (P : Scheme.{u}) [ConnectedSpace P] (f : P ⟶ V.toScheme) [IsFinite f] [Etale f] : ∃ (_ : IsIntegral P) (_ : Algebra X.functionField P.functionField), X.fromSpecOfAlgebraFunctionField P.functionField = P.fromSpecFunctionField ≫ f ≫ V.ι ∧ ∃ e : pullback (X.fromNormalizationIn P.functionField) V.ι ≅ P, e.hom ≫ f = pullback.snd (X.fromNormalizationIn P.functionField) V.ι
